title: compact-journey-heuristics-notebook
content:
Context / goal:
This is a personal scratchpad for a small experiment I want to run around compacting user journeys/threads for the hosted API assistant surface. Aim is to reduce token expansion for multi-step tasks while preserving recall of the important context turns (task goals, constraints, latest state).

High level idea:
- Create a light-weight heuristic "journey snapshot" that can be used as a compressed summary/anchor for long-running sessions.
- Snapshot should be incremental, cheap to compute, and compatible with existing prefix / KV caching.
- Primary use-case: customers with long conversational flows (support agents, copilots) where older turns are low-signal but task-defining metadata must survive.

Design constraints / non-goals:
- Non-goal: full semantic condensation (we're not building an abstractive summarizer here).
- Must be <= ~150 tokens serialized so it helps token budget across model sizes.
- Low-latency: snapshot creation should add <10ms median per-turn overhead in the runtime path (if possible, measured on dev cluster).
- Backward compatible: if a snapshot field is absent, fall back to full-turn replay.

Candidate snapshot schema (heuristic fields, not final JSON):
- task-labels: short list (1-3) of user-intended tasks (extracted via simple classifier + regex).
- latest-entities: top 4 entity tokens and last-seen values (only short tokens).
- constraints: 1-2 lines of explicit constraints (e.g. tone:formal, response-length:short).
- last-action: last system/assistant instruction summary (10-20 tokens).
- freshness-score: timestamp or step-id.

Quick user stories:
- As a small-SaaS user, I want the assistant to remember my project name and billing alias without re-sending unrelated chatter, so I stay within quota.
- As a support agent, I want quick context anchors (issue id, priority, affected services) surfaced so I can answer rapidly after multi-hour breaks.
- As infra engineer, I want the compact snapshot to be optional and toggleable per route so customers can opt into token-savings.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Feature toggle per-route + opt-in header documented in API.
- Snapshot serialized size <= 200 tokens for 95% of sessions in our benchmark dataset.
- End-to-end median latency increase < 15ms for POST /v1/chat with snapshot enabled (dev infra).
- Automated regression test: baseline conversation replay vs snapshot-enabled conversation has <= 6% drop in correctness on a task-completion eval suite (TBD).

Instrumentation / metrics to capture:
- token-savings-per-session (median + p95)
- correctness-delta-on-evals (automated daily job)
- additional-latency-per-turn (p50/p95)
- opt-in adoption rate and opt-out reasons (feedback telemetry)

Rollout plan (sketch):
1) Internal alpha: enable on internal workspace routes only, rough metrics, manual QA (2 weeks).
2) Customer beta: opt-in header + Console toggle for 10 pilot customers; gather feedback and run eval suite (4 weeks).
3) Gradual ramp to everyone, default off. Provide recommendation engine in Redwood Optimize to suggest snapshot for eligible routes (post-beta).

Implementation notes / quick tech ideas:
- Extraction: lightweight transformer classifier (tiny distilled) running in the edge pipeline OR regex+heuristic first-pass.
- Storage: attach snapshot to session metadata (backing store already stores session prefix). Keep snapshot as separate small blob to avoid bloating KV cache.
- Merge strategy: when new snapshot arrives, do prioritized merge: newest constraints overwrite, entity map updated with last-seen.
- Compatibility with KV cache: use snapshot as a prefix override for older KV ranges — need to validate that restore logic in session restore accepts this.

Open questions / risks:
- Risk: snapshots might omit subtle context that the model uses for pragmatic inference -> need focused evals (edge cases).
- How to surface snapshot debug info in Console without leaking user PII? We need redaction + sampling.
- Who owns the classifier model (research vs infra)? Cost of running classifier at high qps.
- Worst-case: snapshot hurts quality for multi-step reasoning tasks (long dependency chains).

Short experiment plan for alpha:
- Pick 3 internal long-running flows (onboarding-demo, billing-convo, support-ticket-thread).
- Implement heuristic extractor (regex + simple slot filler) as a prototype in dev runtime.
- Run A/B: baseline replay vs snapshot replay for 2k simulated sessions; measure token-savings and task success.
- Quick user feedback session with 3 support agents in week 2.

Notes / TODOs (personal):
- [ ] Draft API header spec for opt-in (name: x-rrw-compact-snapshot: true)
- [ ] Prototype serializer (compact key order) and measure bytes on dev models
- [ ] Add unit test for merge strategy edge cases (entity overwrite, stale freshness)
- [ ] Run privacy review checklist: PII detection and redaction rules
- [ ] Book time with Mika to review telemetry schema (metrics naming)
- [ ] Create eval prompt set focusing on multi-step tasks (priority queue: onboarding, billing, multi-step edits)

Notes to self: keep the first iteration simple. The win we're chasing is pragmatic: cut token bills for heavy users while keeping the guardrails for quality. If we can save 12-20% tokens for common long sessions with no meaningful quality drop, this is a product win.

Slack snippets to copy into RFC thread:
- "alpha: snapshot blob attached to session metadata; opt-in via header; heuristic extractor proto in edge lambda; metrics: token-savings, latency, correctness-delta"

End of notebook entry. Will iterate after alpha metrics land.
